title: Aurora threshold analysis workshop notes & benchmarking playbook
body:
Summary:
This doc captures the August 2026 Aurora customer workshop focused on establishing latency/throughput thresholds, end-to-end benchmarking methodology, and a lightweight runbook for a 2-week POC. The objective was to validate whether Redwood Dedicated with a mixed-quantization model bundle could meet Aurora's interactive assistant SLOs: median latency <= 120ms for short queries (<=128 tokens) and p95 <= 300ms for typical conversational loads, while keeping incremental token cost below $0.25 per 1K tokens in steady state.

Workshop attendees and goals:
- Attendees: Maya (SE lead), Diego (infra), Priya (model ops), Noah (customer engineering), Evelyn (solutions architect from Aurora).
- Goals: define load profiles, agree measurement definitions, run baseline microbenchmarks, agree on gating criteria for go/no-go.

Definitions and measurement conventions (agreed):
- Cold-start: first request after process spin-up (no KV cache). Measure cold-start P50/P95 separately.
- Warm steady-state: clients send requests after warmup period; KV/prefix cache populated. Primary SLOs evaluated here.
- Tail-latency percentiles: report p50/p90/p95/p99 for both token-level generation latency (per-token step) and request-level end-to-end time (request arrival to final token emitted).
- Token accounting: we count user input + assistant output tokens for cost calculations.
- Throughput: measured in RPS and tokens/sec. Use steady-state token/sec as cost driver.

Customer workload profile (Aurora):
- 65% short-turn queries: 16-64 tokens input, 32-128 tokens output (chat replies)
- 25% medium turns: 64-256 tokens output
- 10% long-form: >512 tokens (rare; cold-path with fallback options)
- Concurrent active sessions target: 1K users peak; estimated average QPS: 200 sustained, spikes to 600 for 30s every 10 minutes

Benchmark environment and model variants tested:
- Redwood Dedicated pool: 4x A100 80GB nodes (isotropic pool) with optimized serving runtime (triton-like kernels + memory-pinned batching).
- Model variants: Aurora-7B (fp16), Aurora-7B-q4_K (quantized 4-bit), Aurora-13B (fp16), Aurora-13B-q4_K.
- Serving config: max_batch_size=64, batch_timeout=6ms, kv_cache=true for warm runs, stream=false for baseline (non-streaming measurements).
- Client harness: custom Rust harness (github link above) simulating session-level conversational traffic with stochastic inter-arrival (Poisson for base load, short bursts for spikes).

Baseline microbench results (short-query profile, warm steady-state):
- Aurora-7B (fp16): p50=95ms, p90=160ms, p95=210ms, p99=340ms; throughput ~ 1.2M tokens/sec across pool; cost estimate $0.18 per 1K tokens.
- Aurora-7B-q4_K: p50=110ms, p90=190ms, p95=240ms, p99=420ms; throughput ~1.4M tokens/sec; cost estimate $0.12 per 1K tokens.
- Aurora-13B (fp16): p50=160ms, p90=260ms, p95=330ms, p99=540ms; throughput ~900K tokens/sec; cost estimate $0.28 per 1K tokens.
- Aurora-13B-q4_K: p50=190ms, p90=300ms, p95=380ms, p99=700ms; throughput ~1.05M tokens/sec; cost estimate $0.20 per 1K tokens.

Observations from microbenchmarks:
- Quantized variants increase throughput and reduce unit cost, at the expense of higher tail latencies under bursty arrival patterns.
- p99 tails for q4_K variants are amplified by kernel switching overheads and scheduling jitter; p95 targets remained acceptable for 7B quantized.
- The 13B family struggled to meet Aurora's median latency SLO; even q4_K 13B approached cost tolerances but missed p50 by a comfortable margin.

Burst and spike behavior (spike: 600 QPS for 30s):
- Under spikes, observed queue build-up on shared pool when batch_size cap hit. Average request enqueue time increased ~2x; p95 moved up by 40-60% compared to steady-state.
- Mitigations tested: reduce batch_timeout to 3ms (improves p95 by ~8% for short queries but reduces throughput ~6%), enable aggressive autoscale burst (provision 2 extra nodes) which restored tail latency but increased cost by ~14% over baseline.

KV/prefix cache effect:
- Cold-start p95s were 2.1-2.5x warm p95. Customer expected longer cold durations during new session churn; recommended fronting ephemeral cold paths with a cached short-reply model to reduce visible latency.
- For warm steady-state, enabling KV cache reduced average latency by 18-25% for dialog flows with repetition. Cache eviction policy needs to be tuned for 1K concurrent sessions to avoid churn.

Cost modeling (steady-state monthly projection):
- Assumptions: 200 sustained QPS, 30% utilization (observed), 30 days, average tokens per request = 120, token pricing table from Redwood Dedicated unit economics.
- Projected monthly cost (baseline pool + run-time token units):
  - Aurora-7B (fp16): $26,000/month
  - Aurora-7B-q4_K: $17,500/month
  - Aurora-13B (fp16): $40,000/month
  - Aurora-13B-q4_K: $28,000/month
- Recommendation: Aurora target is <$25K/month; 7B-q4_K is the only variant that meets cost target while meeting p95 latency SLO.

Quality vs cost tradeoff tests (regression sampling):
- Ran a 2k-sample evaluation comparing fp16 vs q4_K for hallucination and factuality. q4_K introduced a small increase in placeholder token generation in long-form outputs (~1.8% absolute), concentrated on rare entity-heavy prompts. Customer considered this acceptable given fallback guardrails.

Actionable recommendations and POC plan (2-week):
Week 0 (prep):
- Provision Dedicated pool with 4x A100-80GB + 1 warm standby node. Configure autoscale burst policy for 2 spare nodes. (Owner: Diego)
- Build Rust harness scenarios and seed prompt sets from Aurora production anonymized logs (owner: Noah).
- Confluence: baseline experiment plan + pass/fail gating criteria (owner: Maya).

Week 1 (baseline and tuning):
- Run cold->warm baseline against fp16 and q4_K 7B variants. Capture p50/p95/p99, throughput, utilization. (owners: Priya, Diego)
- Tune batch_timeout/batch_size and measure impact on p95 vs throughput tradeoff. Document recommended config.

Week 2 (burst tests, cost model, quality evals):
- Execute burst spike patterns, autoscale behavior tests, and quantify cost uplift for burst capacity. (owner: Diego)
- Run 2k prompt regression suite to validate quality delta for q4_K. (owner: Priya)
- Finalize runbook and go/no-go recommendation for Aurora. (owner: Maya)

Runbook snippets (quick notes):
- If p95 exceeds agreed threshold during test: first roll back batch_timeout increase, then enable autoscale burst, then route 10% of traffic to a smaller cached model for short replies.
- For persistent p99 excursions: capture full heap/metrics snapshot, open SE pager channel, and isolate whether tail is kernel contention vs network/device saturation.

Open questions for Aurora to decide before POC kickoff:
- Will Aurora accept q4_K production variant given small quality regressions? (business-level acceptance)
- Confirm acceptable cost envelope including burst allowances and SLAs for peak events.
- Any regulatory constraints requiring specific quantization/precision choices?

Appendix: raw sample logs and measurement notes (high level)
- Example perf line: "variant=7B-q4_K node=gp4-03 rps=210 tokens_sec=1.38e6 p95=240ms p99=420ms batch=48"
- JIRA tickets created: JIRA-1234 (POC plan), JIRA-1240 (autoscale tuning), JIRA-1251 (quality eval for q4_K).

Conclusions:
- For Aurora's stated SLOs and cost target, the 7B q4_K variant on a 4x A100 pool is the leading candidate. It meets median/p95 in warm steady-state and stays within cost envelope with acceptable quality tradeoffs. The POC should focus on burst behavior and cache tuning, with a pragmatic fall-back for cold starts (small cached reply model).

Notes to self / workshop fragments (raw):
- "Priya: try kernel pre-warm before spike window"
- "Diego: measure PCIe bandwidth during p99 spikes"
- "Maya: confirm Aurora will accept 2-week data retention for logs"

Next steps: finalize experiment scripts, lock schedule with Aurora for Sept 6 kickoff, circulate this doc to Aurora team, and schedule a short call to confirm q4_K acceptance criteria.
